scope: Features carrying reauditNote were re-audited against Rust source and tests; other feature statuses remain as previously audited. Statuses move only against the acceptance text.

tests.limitations: No live Minecraft, real provider, connector matrix, production deployment, Linux host, or penetration verification.

features.name: Deployment and instance scope
features.current: Rust has protected server-install roots and a server-scoped discovery contract, but no agent installer/adoption flow or persisted instance registry proving existing data stays in place and server_id survives restart.
features.acceptance: Install alongside an existing server without moving its data; preserve server_id across restart.

previous.current: Existing roots, config and instance registry exist; independent process/control-plane identities and tested Windows/Linux parity do not.

features.name: Process lifecycle
features.current: Owned start/stop/kill with generation tracking in Rust. Graceful stop reports an unsupported stop honestly, and force kill is a separate confirmed action. The agent still owns the game process.
features.acceptance: Stop timeout offers a separate confirmed Kill; never silently kills or creates duplicate processes.

previous.current: Start/stop/restart/kill exist, but stop force-kills after ten seconds and control is owned by the agent JVM.

features.name: Independent supervisor and crash continuity
features.current: Opt-in per-server vesta-supervisor owns the game over protected same-account local IPC (no network listener). Agent exit leaves the game running and a new agent adopts the same generation without relaunching; a PID plus native-start-time record blocks duplicate launches and reports an orphaned game after a supervisor crash without killing it. Not yet: save leases, crash-restart policy, readiness, separate OS identities, service install, Linux execution evidence and the failure-drill gate.
features.acceptance: Kill/restart agent while Minecraft stays alive; recover control and journals without replay.

previous.current: The agent owns the game process and shutdown path; no separate supervisor, save-lease continuity, or recovery across agent loss is implemented.

features.name: Startup script adoption and existing services
features.current: Rust launches a configured game process, but does not inspect/adopt original startup scripts, defer takeover until an approved restart, or detect competing restart loops.
features.acceptance: Keep original scripts; take over only on approved restart and detect competing restart loops.

previous.current: Installer/CLI create and control launch artifacts; seamless script inspection/adoption and robust detached-child adapters remain.

features.name: Readiness and crash-loop policy
features.current: Readiness reports starting/ready/degraded from anchored console patterns plus a bounded status ping, log-only when no port is known, in both process modes. Opt-in crash restart in the separate supervisor uses doubling backoff and a durable crash-loop breaker that leaves the game stopped until reset. Not yet: connector readiness signals, durable notifications (F30) and start-on-agent-start.
features.acceptance: Expose starting/ready/degraded accurately; bounded configurable restart after crash, opt-in.

previous.current: Rust reports process lifecycle state, but has no world-readiness/degraded signal or opt-in bounded crash-restart policy.

features.name: Local identity, pairing and device credentials
features.current: Rust has identity bootstrap and policy primitives, but its production local-authority adapter is unavailable; single-use device pairing, per-device revocation, and OS-authorized recovery are not operational.
features.acceptance: Single-use owner pairing, per-device revocation, OS-authorized local recovery.

previous.current: Link codes and bearers exist; canonical device principals, local owner bootstrap and device certificates are missing.

features.name: Minecraft identity and admission adapters
features.current: Minecraft profile proof, whitelist, ban and online-mode admission are implemented in Rust. Binding to device principals is not yet.
features.acceptance: Verified UUID where appropriate; offline mode never treated as trusted online player identity.

previous.current: Session challenge and whitelist reader exist; binding to device principals, bans and policy reconciliation remain.

features.name: Roles, denies, scope and delegation
features.current: Built-in roles, named capabilities with deny composition and scope, and delegation rank tests exist in Rust. Nothing can reach them through an authenticated remote management device yet.
features.acceptance: Owner/Admin locally granted only; deny wins, bounded delegation and expiry tested.

previous.current: Named capabilities exist within numeric levels derived from OP/permission nodes, not independent Vesta role assignments.

features.name: Operation confirmation and security audit
features.current: Structured audit records with bounded fields are stored in SQLite. Exact-target operation confirmations and receipts exist, and file-change intents are journaled before effects. There is no remote confirmation flow or protected audit export yet.
features.acceptance: Actor/target/revision-bound confirmation; sensitive mutations fail if audit cannot persist.

previous.current: Ordinary logs exist, but no durable exact-target confirmations or protected structured audit subsystem found.

features.name: TLS, stable server identity and device authentication
features.current: TLS 1.2 or later with configured PEM material, validated hot reload, and the active fingerprint in discovery. Mutual TLS device lifecycle is not implemented.
features.acceptance: Bootstrap works without client cert; all management requires device authentication, including via proxy.

previous.current: TLS material and certificate fingerprint API exist; mutual TLS device lifecycle and renewal-safe identity separation remain.

features.name: Vault, password hashing and credential lifecycle
features.current: Pack passwords are Argon2id-hashed with SQLite verifiers and revision tracking. There is no vault and no device credential lifecycle.
features.acceptance: Argon2id for Vesta passwords; OS-protected recoverable secrets; no normal secret export.

previous.current: MVP hashes human passwords with salted SHA-256 and persists plaintext security.password; no protected vault found.

features.name: Abuse, request and storage limits
features.current: Rust bounds HTTP request bodies, shared jobs/downloads, and upload/storage operations, but not coordinated CPU, memory, staging, and recovery-reachability budgets across all workloads.
features.acceptance: Bound input, memory, CPU, concurrent work and staging; recovery remains reachable.

previous.current: HTTP/auth token buckets exist; transfer/storage quotas and coordinated resource budgets are incomplete.

features.name: Public/versioned API and event contract
features.current: Versioned /api/v2 pack API covers status, password and Minecraft authentication, tickets, artifacts and realtime notices. v1 returns 410 and /manage returns 403. The management API is absent.
features.acceptance: Version negotiation; resumable event cursors with gaps; idempotent mutation contract.

previous.current: HTTP/WebSocket and legacy TCP messages exist; target OpenAPI, durable cursors, idempotency and consistent errors remain.

features.name: 10,000-line live console buffer
features.current: Rust captures a 10,000-line, 2 MiB bounded console ring with bounded pages and viewer-independent drains, and tests those limits/concurrency; full slow-viewer and no-duplicate-retained-game-log acceptance is not established.
features.acceptance: 10,000-line cap, bounded bytes and slow-viewer protection; no retained duplicate game logs.

previous.current: Bounded in-memory console ring is present; focused existing ConsoleBuffer tests passed. This does not verify supervisor continuity.

features.name: Game-log catch-up and player reconciliation
features.current: Rust parses live player-list observations and rejects malformed or contradictory counts, but has no persistent game-log offset/rotation reconciliation; missing-log unknown state and the no-sleep/no-replayed-moderation guarantee are absent.
features.acceptance: Missing logs mark unknown; uncertain count never triggers sleep or replayed moderation.

previous.current: Live list-command parsing exists; persistent log offsets, rotation/gap reconciliation and reliable absence are missing.

features.name: File confinement and protected roots
features.current: Confinement refuses protected names, alias and reparse targets, uses no-replace renames, and journals writes. Same-account ancestor races remain a residual limitation.
features.acceptance: Race-aware confinement for existing/new paths, links, junctions and every file route.

previous.current: Basic sanitization/real-path checks exist; creation through symlink parents and protected-root coverage need hardening.

features.name: File editing, trash, archives and transfers
features.current: Trash with quotas and retention, optimistic writes, resumable uploads staged in protected state, mkdir and rename, and provider content installs exist. These are library APIs with no network entry point. Archives and SFTP are not implemented.
features.acceptance: Recoverable bounded trash; revision-based text edits; safe archives and disk preflight.

previous.current: Read/write/delete exist with temporary-file replacement. No complete trash, optimistic edits, archives or resumable transfer engine found.

features.name: SFTP service and unified file policy
features.current: SFTP is declared future work; no Rust SFTP service integrates file operations with principals, scopes, quotas, locks, trash, and audit.
features.acceptance: Optional SFTP uses the same principals, scopes, quotas, locks, trash and audit.

previous.current: No SFTP subsystem or dependency located.

features.name: Content sources and safe server updates
features.current: Modrinth and CurseForge installs are resolved server-side, use an allowlisted HTTPS host, verify hashes, and commit through a journaled write. This is library only. Restart activation is not implemented.
features.acceptance: Refuse hashless arbitrary URL; stage server code until approved process exit; no automatic restart.

previous.current: Live install/remove supports byte hashing; provider-resolution, expected-hash verification and restart activation are not complete.

features.name: Separate hosted client-pack workspace
features.current: Pack snapshots come from explicitly configured sources, with native catalogue references for platform packs. Scanning is selected-directory only. There is no separate workspace UI.
features.acceptance: Dedicated draft/overrides workspace; no automatic server-to-pack copying.

previous.current: MVP can host platform/archive sources, but scan mode and generated packs read the live server tree.

features.name: Vesta Pack schema and provider references
features.current: Rust defines and tests the VestaIndex v1 projection, catalogue/source references, and hash fields, but fixed provider-ID/hash compatibility and a complete unavailable-source failure contract are not verified against the full launcher schema.
features.acceptance: Existing VestaIndex compatible; fixed provider IDs/hashes; clear unavailable-source failure.

previous.current: Vesta index builder includes revision/minimum revision and external references; launcher-compatible schema fixtures need expansion.

features.name: Pack build, publication and scheduled release
features.current: Durable publication checks revisions, and pruning is quarantined and recovered on restart. Pack-only HTTPS and realtime notices are served. There is no scheduled release and no trusted publish entry point in serve.
features.acceptance: Publish complete verified artifact immediately or at explicit time; only one public current revision.

previous.current: Archive builder and configured revisions exist; durable publication transaction, automatic revision increment and scheduled activation remain.

features.name: Pack policy, minimum version and authorization
features.current: Rust implements pack access and release policy/revision primitives, but there is no complete optional/required release lifecycle or demonstrated revoked-management fallback to public policy.
features.acceptance: Optional/required release choices; revoked management falls back to public pack policy only.

previous.current: Capabilities and revision fields exist; complete independent pack policy and minimum-version lifecycle remain.

features.name: Ignore policies and pack symlink safety
features.current: Snapshots refuse links and reparse points and enforce protected names. Configurable ignore policies are not implemented.
features.acceptance: Pack/file/backup ignore policies stay separate; constrained links have explicit manifest warnings.

previous.current: Independent target ignore rules and per-revision symlink consent protocol not located.

features.name: Backup repositories and retention
features.current: Backup repositories, encrypted recovery export, retention, and working-space reserve are declared future work; installer file-copy protections are not a runtime backup/history subsystem.
features.acceptance: Opt-in local/NAS/S3 encrypted repositories, recovery export, retention and working-space reserve.

previous.current: Installer copy/backup options are not a runtime restic repository/history subsystem.

features.name: Online backup consistency and save lease
features.current: Online backup coordination and autosave/save-lease cleanup are not implemented; plugin-based consistency remains future work.
features.acceptance: Flush acknowledgement; independent same-generation autosave cleanup; honest plugin consistency.

previous.current: No online-backup coordinator, crash-safe autosave lease or snapshot helper found.

features.name: Restore, inspection and recovery exports
features.current: Owner-confirmed restore, pre-restore backup, stopped-game enforcement, scoped inspection, and recovery exports are not implemented; backups/recovery are future work.
features.acceptance: Owner-confirmed restore, pre-restore backup, stopped game, scoped inspection, no automatic restore.

previous.current: No verified manual restore workflow or encrypted complete recovery export found.

features.name: Durable operations, locks and recovery journals
features.current: The operation runner has claim ownership, replay and confirmation receipts. File intents and prune quarantine are recovered on restart. No remote management transport drives it yet.
features.acceptance: Survive launcher/agent loss; safe-point cancellation; generation-bound restart and no blind replay.

previous.current: HTTP actions are synchronous/ephemeral; no durable operation store or resource-lock recovery found.

features.name: Schedules and typed sequential workflows
features.current: Durable scheduled typed workflows, authority rechecks, and missed-run policy are absent; operation queue scheduling is not an owner workflow scheduler.
features.acceptance: Sequential steps/conditions/delays; authority rechecked; configurable missed-run policy.

previous.current: Session cleanup timers are not an owner scheduler; durable typed workflows/presets absent.

features.name: Notification inbox and optional delivery
features.current: Rust emits transient realtime update events, but has no durable per-principal inbox/read state, offline retrieval, or email/Discord/webhook retry delivery; Discord is future work.
features.acceptance: Per-principal read state; offline retrieval; bounded optional email/Discord/webhook retries.

previous.current: Push update events exist, but no durable per-account inbox/delivery subsystem found.

features.name: Maintenance, whitelist overlay and hooks
features.current: Rust has a whitelist read adapter, but no maintenance overlay or journalled reconciliation that preserves owner edits and survives crashes.
features.acceptance: Connector overlay or journalled whitelist reconciliation; no stale overwrite of owner edits.

previous.current: Whitelist read adapter exists; temporary maintenance restrictions and crash-safe reconciliation are absent.

features.name: Sleep, offline status and wake-on-join
features.current: Sleep/status packet handling and a rate-limited join-wake coordinator are absent; MOTD/sleep behavior is declared future work.
features.acceptance: Never wake on ping; join wake rate-limited; honest retry/startup/offline responses.

previous.current: No game-port sleep/status responder or wake coordinator located.

features.name: MOTD/settings placeholders and lifecycle presentation
features.current: Rust has validated host configuration and pack status responses, but no online/offline MOTD templates, launcher lifecycle presentation, or state-aware live-change/restart reporting; MOTD work is future scope.
features.acceptance: Online/offline templates; status in launcher; live changes state reload/restart requirements.

previous.current: Static descriptor/status exists; structured live/offline templates and state-aware game responses are absent.

features.name: Typed moderation and online player management
features.current: Rust can query live players and parse typed player observations, but does not expose typed moderator actions/history; console operations are not a safe typed moderation interface.
features.acceptance: Moderator typed actions only by default; console authority never impersonates player.

previous.current: Online players and unrestricted console exist; separate safe moderation endpoints/history remain.

features.name: Metrics, diagnostics and resource budgets
features.current: Rust exposes process lifecycle and live-player observations, but no unknown-labelled metrics, configurable 24h/30d/1y metrics retention, or redacted manual export; metrics retention was declared future work.
features.acceptance: Unknown metrics labelled; 24h/30d/1y retention tiers configurable; redacted manual export.

previous.current: Basic process/status/list snapshots exist; TPS adapters, storage-limited retention and redacted bundles remain.

features.name: Structured server configuration
features.current: Rust validates host TOML and game launch configuration, but has no schema-backed server.properties/JVM/ban/loader editing with preserved edits and live/reload/restart impact reporting; external database provisioning is absent.
features.acceptance: Validate and preserve edits; report live/reload/restart; no external database provisioning.

previous.current: Security TOML editor exists; server.properties/JVM/ban/loader schema-backed edits and apply modes are incomplete.

features.name: SQLite state, repair and pending changes
features.current: Schema migrations v1 to v11 have upgrade tests from committed versions. The state database is transactional and can be backed up. There is no interactive repair tool or pending-change UI.
features.acceptance: Local WAL database, safe exports/migrations; corruption fails closed; desired/effective state separate.

previous.current: No SQLite dependency/state layer or durable pending-change reconciliation located.

features.name: OS isolation and optional sandbox profiles
features.current: Rust applies platform protection to agent state paths, but no plugin-versus-agent/supervisor access isolation or optional sandbox/resource profile is implemented, and portable-mode warnings are absent.
features.acceptance: Plugins cannot read/write agent state or supervisor control; portable mode warns honestly.

previous.current: Service scripts exist; verified separate game/control identities and sandbox/resource-limit profiles remain.

features.name: Java runtime and compatibility matrix
features.current: Rust launches the game as a separate process and can probe a configured Java runtime, with loader/runtime planning tests; a tested adapter-capability compatibility matrix across game/loader/platform combinations is not established.
features.acceptance: Game runtime independent of agent runtime; adapter capabilities match tested combinations.

previous.current: Custom Java/JVM arguments and loader release matrix exist; guided game-runtime provisioning and 1.7+ test matrix remain.

features.name: Network discovery, NAT and optional proxy setup
features.current: Rust implements versioned server-scoped discovery and TLS transport, but no LAN/direct/VPN/proxy reachability diagnostics, CGNAT diagnosis, consented probes, or NAT setup; NAT/proxy setup is declared future work.
features.acceptance: Local/LAN/direct/VPN/proxy coexist; CGNAT diagnosed; probe consent; no required relay.

previous.current: Server descriptor/address utilities exist; end-to-end reachability diagnostics, ACME and reviewed proxy setup remain.

features.name: Signed agent/connector updates
features.current: Signed update metadata/artifacts, rollback protection, and stopped-only supervisor activation are not implemented; signed updates are future work.
features.acceptance: Signed metadata/artifacts; no automatic restart; supervisor activates only while stopped.

previous.current: Distribution packaging exists, not signed rollback-protected updates and approved activation.

features.name: Installer, CLI and nonintrusive uninstall
features.current: Rust server-install library (crates/vesta-server-install) provides approval-gated installs for Vanilla, Paper, Folia and Purpur, download-only Fabric and Quilt bundles, verified transfers, a bounded execution workspace and receipts. Forge and NeoForge, managed Java, the setup walkthrough and uninstall are not implemented, and the Java one-liner scripts still perform the real install.
features.acceptance: Preserve worlds/scripts/settings; opt-in connector; secure defaults and advanced answers.

previous.current: Windows/Linux installers, registry/control CLI and service helpers exist; complete secure walkthrough/connector setup remain.

features.name: Discord status/linking and integration presets
features.current: Discord identity linking, status, notifications, and delivery presets are not implemented; Discord is declared future work.
features.acceptance: Optional channel-configured safe status/notifications; no remote Owner/Admin grant.

previous.current: No Discord bot, identity linkage or outbound delivery provider located.

features.name: Declarative extensions and opt-in telemetry
features.current: No declarative extension registry or product telemetry-consent implementation is present; the Rust agent does not provide these acceptance behaviors.
features.acceptance: No arbitrary code in privileged agent; no product telemetry unless explicitly enabled.

previous.current: No target schema-extension registry/telemetry consent implementation located.

features.name: Velocity, multi-server, relay and host protocol extensions
features.current: The Rust protocol supports a server-scoped discovery contract, but Velocity/multi-server/relay/host extensions remain later topology work and are not initial blockers.
features.acceptance: Preserve public server-scoped protocol; do not make later hosting capabilities initial blockers.

previous.current: Future topology/features; initial scope is one independently secured Java server per agent.

phases.title: Baseline & contracts
phases.gate: Requirements traceability, threat model, target schemas and migration boundaries accepted.

phases.title: Durable foundation
phases.gate: SQLite, operations/locks, audit, confirmations and protocol failure recovery pass fault tests.

phases.title: Identity & security
phases.gate: Independent roles, devices, local recovery, protected vault and all transport authorization pass.

phases.title: Supervisor & adoption
phases.gate: Agent loss leaves game running; no silent force kill; save cleanup and platform permissions proven.

phases.title: Files & content
phases.gate: HTTPS/SFTP share path policy, trash, budgets and staged JAR activation; adversarial file tests pass.

phases.title: Client-pack hosting
phases.gate: Separate workspace, compatible manifest, durable publication/revisions and pack policies pass.

phases.title: Backups & recovery
phases.gate: Online cleanup survives agent loss; repositories verify; restores are manual and storage-safe.

phases.title: Automation & community ops
phases.gate: Durable workflows/inbox, metrics, moderation, maintenance and sleep operate with honest capabilities.

phases.title: Distribution & release
phases.gate: Secure installer, signed updates, networking diagnostics and full Windows/Linux release gates pass.

phases.title: Later extensions
phases.gate: Separately scoped proposals only; not required to call the single-server release complete.

previousSnapshot.scope: Planning only. Launcher examined only for shared VestaIndex schema; no launcher implementation audit or changes.

tests.source: Existing JUnit XML reports dated 2026-10-04 after core/wrapper rerun.
tests.limitations: No live Minecraft, connector matrix, production deployment, Linux host, or security penetration verification.
